A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from DriveMM to RoboTron-Drive, and all supplied pages are readable. v1 includes Appendices A-C; v4 ends after the references despite mentioning supplementary material. Judgments about absent content concern the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v1 reports original six-benchmark evaluations, BDD-X transfer results, component and mixed-dataset ablations, and qualitative model outputs in Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds DRAMA and DriveBench evaluations, curriculum controls, and nuScenes planning results.

M1.justification: The SigLIP/MLP/Llama architecture, perspective-aware prompt, QA augmentation and standardization, and four-stage curriculum remain unchanged. The planning experiment applies task-specific fine-tuning without specifying a new component, objective, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: v4 retains the six principal driving datasets and BDD-X, adds zero-shot evaluation on DRAMA and DriveBench, and introduces nuScenes trajectory-planning fine-tuning and evaluation. This substantially broadens transfer coverage and evaluation beyond the original QA-oriented benchmarks.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds RoboTron-Drive-Zero while retaining existing comparators. New comparisons include Dolphins-7B, DriveLM-7B, Qwen2-VL variants, InterVL2-8B, GPT-4o and human references on DriveBench, plus UniAD and VAD-Base for planning.

E3.justification: New protocols include GPT-4o evaluation on DRAMA, DriveBench's standard evaluation, and open-loop planning on nuScenes validation data using L2 error and collision rates at 1, 2 and 3 seconds. Ablation controls also change: prompt removal is tested against the full model, and curriculum training is compared with mixed-complexity training from the start.

E4.justification: v4 expands curriculum analysis with mixed-training and intermediate-pretraining controls and adds the no-AD-fine-tuning baseline. QA and mixed-dataset ablations are retained, while the prompt ablation is revised. Most of v1's 16 qualitative case studies are absent; Figure S14 survives as v4 Figure 4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The specialist upper and lower bounds in v4 Figure 1 summarize different models' scores, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All existing Table 3 values and the BDD-X results remain unchanged. v4 adds substantial result blocks, including DRAMA 53.32, a reported DriveBench average of 61.06, new ablation results, and planning averages of 0.33 m L2 error and 0.26% collision. These are newly reported evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v4 removes Section 3.2's explicit tensor-domain definitions, encoder/projector equations, and autoregressive probability factorization from v1 Equations 2-4, replacing them with a brief prose description. Equation 1 remains; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract extends its stated zero-shot performance scope from one unseen dataset to three. The central contributions remain the all-in-one driving model, comprehensive multi-benchmark evaluation, and curriculum training.

C2.justification: v4 adds an interpretation attributing curriculum gains to progressively increasing task and data difficulty and emphasizes its AD-specific curriculum. It also frames comparisons more explicitly around zero-shot versus AD-fine-tuned models. The existing generalization and mixed-dataset interpretations largely remain, without a substantial new limitations discussion.

D1.justification: The supplied v4 omits v1's detailed learning rates, batch sizes, epochs, training-data composition, frame counts, dataset sample counts, and exact augmentation prompt. Some architecture details move from Appendix A into Section 4.1. Newly disclosed information includes 32 A100 GPUs and stage durations of 1, 26, 90 and 60 hours.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations including DriveBench, Dolphins, Qwen2-VL, UniAD, VAD and several multimodal or robotics works, while some appendix-linked data references disappear. The related-work narrative and claimed novelty of a comprehensive generalist driving model remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper is renamed throughout, architecture and dataset descriptions are compressed, experimental-setting subsections are combined, and ablation discussion is reorganized. Acknowledgements are added, but most introduction, methodology, and conclusion prose retains the earlier narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1's transfer plot is redesigned around three datasets, Table 3 is regrouped into zero-shot and fine-tuned models, and the ablation displays are split and expanded. New DriveBench and planning tables appear. Figure S14 becomes a compact main-text Figure 4, while the remaining supplementary figures and prompt table are absent.

improvement.justification: Broader transfer evaluations and curriculum controls strengthen empirical support, and separating zero-shot from fine-tuned comparisons improves clarity. However, v4 loses substantial reproducibility information available in v1 and introduces an internal inconsistency: identical scores average 60.39 in Table 6 but 60.23 in Table 7. These material evidence gains and documentation/reliability losses do not establish a confident net improvement.
